comments.author: Aether-
comments.body:
1. One responsibility per file — the doc line needs an "and" (registry and discovery inventory), and it bundles three 
      jobs (registry types/data, id inference, FS discovery walker). Per the rule, that's a split, not one file.
   2. Pure core / impure shell — the std::fs walker sits in the same file as the pure registry types and pure 
      infer/normalize helpers.

comments.pr_title: Add LLM persona UX regression harness
comments.author: Aether-
comments.body:
1. One responsibility per file — clearly violated. In one file: the enums/descriptors (PersonaDriver, PersonaSuite, 
      PersonaId, PersonaScenarioResult, ...), the persona catalog data (persona_catalog), the suite runner (run_suite), 
      the LLM subprocess driver (Command::new(...).spawn() at L751), report file I/O (fs::create_dir_all/fs::write at 
      L465-469), and report explanation (explain_report). That's at least 4-5 responsibilities.

   2. Should be a directory module. Per "when a responsibility grows sub-parts, it becomes a directory module that 
      recursively follows the same shape," 1367 lines with an LLM driver + probes + reporting should be persona_ux/ with 
      catalog.rs, runner.rs, driver.rs (impure subprocess), report.rs (impure fs), and pure types.rs. Right now it's a 
      flat persona_ux.rs.

   3. Pure core / impure shell not separated. Subprocess spawning (Command/Stdio) and fs::write sit alongside the pure 
      type/catalog/probe logic. The exemplar keeps side effects on their own documented path.
